solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Tan forehead and backside in sun (5)

indicatorNotes.backside in: a word's backside is its rear end, so only the last letter of sun is wanted

annotation.surface: A sunbather checks where the tan has taken: face and bottom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tan' looks like a verb about sunbathing; here it is the colour, and 'backside' is the end of a word rather than a body part.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain colour synonym: tan names a yellowish shade within the brown family.

entries.clue: Question: “And what have you included in support for hopeless organisation?” (6,4)

indicatorNotes.included in: what is included in something sits inside it, so the question goes within the support

blocks.note: a base is what supports something; it opens around the rest
etc = and so on, and what have you

annotation.surface: An interviewer quizzes someone about what they packed into a failing charity's support.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the clue look like a snatch of dialogue; only 'for' links it to the definition at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a basket case is anything, a person or an organisation, too far gone to function or be saved.

entries.clue: Needing to be paid over the phone for poem (3)

indicatorNotes.over the phone: on a phone call you only hear a word, so its sound counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: money owed is money still needing to be paid

annotation.surface: A debt collector rings about a bill still needing to be paid.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a phone call about money, which hides that the phone is only there to tell you to listen.
annotation.definitionFit: A kind-for-category definition: an ode is a lyric poem, usually addressed to its subject.

entries.clue: Guilty party working around bit of California (6)

indicatorNotes.around: something turned around faces the other way, so ON reads backwards

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
a small coin, a bit of the money used in California

annotation.surface: Police close in on a culprit active near the Californian coast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bit of California' tempts you to take a letter such as C or CA; it is a small coin spent there. The answer is a rare word, the opposite of innocent.
annotation.definitionFit: A rare dictionary sense: nocent means guilty, and as a noun a guilty person, from the same Latin root as innocent.

entries.clue: Where Leviticus comes with simple instructions (2,7)

blocks.note: Leviticus is the third book of the Old Testament; think of the book beside it
following step-by-step instructions, as in a children's colouring kit

annotation.surface: A Bible scholar says Leviticus is easy to follow.
annotation.walkthrough: Numbers is the fourth book of the Bible, so Leviticus comes by Numbers; painting by numbers is the second sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a positional one in the order of Bible books, and an idiom for doing something mechanically, step by step.

entries.clue: President Trump originally consumed food using two teeth (9)

indicatorNotes.originally: a word's origin is where it starts, so take the first letter of Trump

annotation.surface: A news item on a president's table manners at a state dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pairs two presidents; only Biden is used whole, and Trump gives just its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical sense: bidentate means having two teeth, and in chemistry a molecule gripping at two points.

entries.clue: English poet’s contradictory answers (5)

blocks.note: the author of the ballad The Highwayman
a negative reply and a positive one, back to back

annotation.surface: A critic complains that a poet keeps changing his mind.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the poet is contradictory answers. Alfred Noyes wrote The Highwayman; split his name and it reads NO YES.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a proper name, Alfred Noyes, and a literal run-together of two opposite replies.

entries.clue: Maybe walrus in Alaska is compelled to feel pain (8)

blocks.note: to ache is to feel pain

annotation.surface: A walrus on the Alaskan ice is suffering.
annotation.walkthrough: A walrus here is a droopy walrus moustache, and 'in Alaska' asks for the American spelling without the O.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example with a regional twist: the walrus is a style of moustache, spelt the American way.

entries.clue: European vehicle being reported in passing (11)

indicatorNotes.reported: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so only the sound counts

annotation.surface: A news line about a foreign lorry mentioned as it drove by.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In passing' reads as 'incidentally'; 'in' is only a link and 'passing' is the noun, the act of fading away.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: evanescence is the quality of vanishing quickly, a passing out of existence.

entries.clue: Second newspaper claiming love is “sentimental” (4)

indicatorNotes.claiming: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the newspaper holds the love inside

blocks.note: love = nil = O, as in tennis

annotation.surface: A rival paper sneers that another's love story is mawkish.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'sentimental' look like a word being quoted by the paper; it is simply the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone soft is easily moved to tender feelings.

entries.clue: Event to go in school diary regularly (6,3)

indicatorNotes.in: 'to go in school' puts the going inside the abbreviation for school
indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter of diary

blocks.note: SCH is the standard abbreviation for school
to go is a euphemism for to urinate

annotation.surface: A date for the school calendar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To go in' reads as 'to be entered'; 'to go' is instead the toilet euphemism. A speech day is a British school prize-giving.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: speech day is one particular event, the annual school gathering with speeches and prizes.

entries.clue: Ruckus about having a stolen muffler (5)

indicatorNotes.about: turned about means facing the other way, so the word reads backwards
indicatorNotes.having a stolen: something stolen is taken away, so one A goes missing

blocks.note: a fracas is a noisy quarrel

annotation.surface: A scuffle breaks out over a stolen muffler.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stolen muffler' reads as one item of theft; the break falls after 'stolen', and the muffler is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a muffler is a warm scarf wound around the neck.

entries.clue: As a result of embarrassing blunder, encourage unity with science fiction expert (3,2,4,4)

annotation.definition: As a result of embarrassing blunder
annotation.definitionNote: The answer is the state you are left in as a result of an embarrassing blunder, not a preposition phrase.

blocks.note: to egg on is to encourage

annotation.surface: After a gaffe, a manager tries to rally the team around a sci-fi specialist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unity' is used in its mathematical sense, the number one, not togetherness.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone left with egg on their face looks foolish because of their own mistake.

entries.clue: I got lineages disentangled? (11)

indicatorNotes.disentangled: what is disentangled is pulled apart and laid out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone proudly announces they have sorted out their family tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The I is the speaker, not fodder: read whole, the clue is the family-tree researcher describing their job, and the question mark flags the double duty.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue is exactly what a family-tree researcher says of their work: untangling lineages.

entries.clue: Erotic display in bar that Chas has entered (10)

indicatorNotes.has entered: whoever has entered a place is inside it, so the Chas go inside the bar

blocks.note: a stripe is a bar of colour
cha is slang for tea, so chas are teas

annotation.surface: A man called Chas has walked into a bar where an erotic show is on.
annotation.walkthrough: Chas looks like a man's name; it is the plural of cha, British slang for tea.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the act is an erotic performance of slowly undressing.

entries.clue: What may contain ice cream and cold drink? (4)

blocks.note: as in 'may I get you one?'

annotation.surface: A café menu question: something to hold an ice cream and a chilled drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ice cream and cold drink' reads as one list of things to hold; the split falls after ice cream.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the wafer cone is the edible holder for a scoop of ice cream.

entries.clue: Put coat on dog, according to Spooner, and get to play more golf? (4,3,3)

indicatorNotes.according to Spooner: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so do the same

blocks.note: to cake is to coat thickly; a mutt is a dog; swap the C and M sounds

annotation.surface: A golfer dresses the dog for the weather and hopes for more rounds.
annotation.walkthrough: In golf tournaments the field is cut after two rounds, and only those above the line play the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A golf idiom: players who make the cut stay in the tournament for the final rounds.

entries.clue: Immortalises model: see insert (9)

indicatorNotes.model: as a verb, to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

annotation.surface: An editor's note: a model's picture is in the insert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun followed by a caption; it is the verb telling you to reshape the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to make something eternal is to immortalise it.

entries.clue: Possibly John Terry fed up on big night out after having head shaved (8)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom upwards
indicatorNotes.after having head shaved: a shaved head has lost its top, so the first letter goes
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

blocks.note: a bender is a drinking spree

annotation.surface: A footballer's night on the town and a fresh haircut make the tabloids.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' reads as bored; it is FED written upwards. John Terry captained Chelsea and England as a centre-back.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: John Terry is one famous footballer who played in that position, hence 'Possibly'.

entries.clue: Desire to act foolishly, at first, punching leg continually (5,5)

indicatorNotes.at first: take what comes first in foolishly, its opening letter
indicatorNotes.punching: a punch breaks into something, so the F forces its way between the two words

blocks.note: a leg of a journey is a stage

annotation.surface: An urge to play the fool makes someone keep kicking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desire to act foolishly' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'act'.
annotation.definitionFit: A dictionary phrase: stage fever is a longing to go on the stage as an actor.

entries.clue: Opposed to insect being skinned (or insect being skinned twice) (4)

indicatorNotes.being skinned: skinning strips the outside, so the first and last letters come off

annotation.surface: A protester objects to insects being flayed.
annotation.walkthrough: The bracket gives a second parse: insect = ANT, and 'being' skinned twice loses BE and NG in turn to leave I.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anti, as a preposition, means against or opposed to.

entries.clue: Drunk with problem somersaulting — an important indicator in test (6)

indicatorNotes.somersaulting: a somersault turns you head over heels, so SUM is flipped

blocks.note: a sum is a maths problem

annotation.surface: A tipsy candidate wrestles with a tough question in an exam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Indicator' is the chemistry sense, a dye that changes colour; it does not signal a clue mechanism here.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint at a set phrase: the dye is the key indicator in the acid test that bears its name.

entries.clue: Cocksure cook I’ve confronted (4-9)

indicatorNotes.cook: to cook figures is to rework them, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A cocky chef boasts about having stood up to someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cook' reads as the chef doing the boasting; it is the verb telling you to rework the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: cocksure describes someone far too sure of themselves.

entries.clue: Setter in bed shows heavenly body (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the setter lying in bed is inside it, so ME goes within the bed's letters

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
the setter refers to themself as me

annotation.surface: A setter lying in bed spots something in the night sky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like a dog or a sunset; it is the puzzle's author speaking of themself.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: this icy wanderer with a tail is one kind of heavenly body.

entries.clue: Prima donna keen to go north (4)

indicatorNotes.to go north: in a down clue, north is upward, so the word is read bottom to top

annotation.surface: A star singer eager to tour up north.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a singer's travel plans; 'north' only works as a direction because this is a down clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses share one word: the leading lady of an opera, and a temperamental star.

entries.clue: Story of Homer Simpson perhaps abandoning son and daughter on island (5)

indicatorNotes.abandoning: to abandon is to leave behind, so the S for son is left out
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

annotation.surface: Homer Simpson walks out on his children to live on an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Homer Simpson' reads as one name; split it, and Homer is the Greek poet while Simpson points to Lisa.
annotation.definitionFit: A title definition: this is the epic of the Trojan War credited to the Greek poet Homer.

entries.clue: Channels providing news service aimed to reform (4,5)

indicatorNotes.to reform: to re-form is to form again, so the letters take a new shape

annotation.surface: A reforming broadcaster's news service.
annotation.walkthrough: 'News service' looks like one phrase; news belongs to the definition and service is the Mass.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: newspapers, television and radio are the channels through which news reaches everyone.

entries.clue: Spot fish (3)

blocks.note: a small blob, as of paint

annotation.walkthrough: 'Spot' could also be a verb, to see, which leads nowhere; it is the noun, a small daub.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a small daub or spot of something, and a flatfish related to the plaice.

entries.clue: Complaint from old king wanting uniform? Yes (9)

indicatorNotes.wanting: wanting means lacking, so the king goes without the U

blocks.note: Uniform is U in the radio alphabet; drop it

annotation.surface: An old king without his uniform grumbles, and a courtier agrees.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' sounds like a grievance; it is a medical complaint.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a complaint is any ailment, and this painful inflammation of the joints is one.

entries.clue: Qualified to track small antelope (5)

indicatorNotes.to track: to track something is to follow behind it, so the word for qualified comes after S

annotation.surface: A trained hunter follows a little antelope.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a hunt, which makes 'to track' look like the hunter's verb; it only places the pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the sable is a large black African antelope with sweeping horns.
